'''Zhiwei Yun''' ({{lang-zh|s=恽之玮|p=Yùn Zhīwěi}}; born September 1982) is a Chinese-born American mathematician and writer. He is a Professor of Mathematics at [[MIT]] specializing in [[number theory]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[representation theory]], with a particular focus on the [[Langlands program]].

He was previously a [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 2010 to 2012, assistant professor then associate professor at Stanford University from 2012 to 2016, and professor at Yale University from 2016 to 2017.

==Early life and education==
Yun was born in [[Changzhou|Changzhou, China]].<ref name=birth>{{cite web | url=http://pkunews.pku.edu.cn/xwzh/2012-08/30/content_250548.htm | title=北京大学校友恽之玮获2012年"拉马努金"奖 | date=30 August 2012}}</ref> As a high schooler, he participated in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 2000; he received a gold medal with a perfect score.<ref name=gold>{{Cite web | url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=5950 | title=International Mathematical Olympiad}}</ref> Yun received his bachelor's degree from [[Peking University]] in 2004. In 2009, he received his Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]], under the direction of [[Robert MacPherson (mathematician)|Robert MacPherson]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Zhiwei Yun|url=https://stanford.edu/~zwyun/CVcurrent.pdf|publisher=Stanford University|access-date=2 September 2016|archive-date=15 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915063319/http://stanford.edu/~zwyun/CVcurrent.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=142226 "Zhiwei Yun"], ''[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]''. Retrieved on 4 December 2016.</ref>

==Work==
His collaborations with [[Zhang Wei (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]], [[Xinyi Yuan]] and [[Xinwen Zhu]] have received attention in publications such as [[Quanta Magazine]] and [[Business Insider]].<ref>[https://www.quantamagazine.org/20151208-four-mathematicians/ "Math Quartet Joins Forces on Unified Theory"], ''[[Quanta Magazine]]''. Retrieved on 4 December 2016.</ref><ref>[http://www.businessinsider.com/math-quartet-joins-forces-on-unified-theory-2016-2 "Math Quartet Joins Forces on Unified Theory"], ''[[Business Insider]]''. Retrieved on 4 December 2016.</ref> In particular, his work with [[Zhang Wei (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]] on the [[Taylor expansion]] of L-functions is "already being hailed as one of the most exciting breakthroughs in an important area of number theory in the last 30 years."

Yun also made substantial contributions towards the global [[Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture]].

==Awards==
Yun was awarded the [[SASTRA Ramanujan Prize]] in 2012 for his "fundamental contributions to several areas that lie at the interface of representation theory, algebraic geometry and number theory."<ref name="SASTRA">{{cite web|title=ZHIWEI YUN TO RECEIVE 2012 SASTRA RAMANUJAN PRIZE|url=http://sas.sastra.edu/ramanujan/Ramanujan-Awards.php|publisher=Sastra University|access-date=2 September 2016|archive-date=10 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510043504/http://sas.sastra.edu/ramanujan/Ramanujan-Awards.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In December 2017, he was awarded the [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics|2018 New Horizons In Mathematics Prize]] together with Wei Zhang, Aaron Naber and [[Maryna Viazovska]].

He was included in the 2019 class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to geometry, number theory, and representation theory, including his construction of motives with exceptional Galois groups".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2019 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref> In 2019 he received the [[Morningside Medal]] jointly with [[Xinwen Zhu]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/content/show/92-246.html |title=Morningside Medal 2019 |access-date=2019-08-26 |archive-date=2019-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826095759/http://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/content/show/92-246.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
